text:
alex: Seeing intermittent 150-300ms KV-hit stalls on master after the kernel-selector change. Want an nsys recipe to compare old vs new builds without ending up with 10GB traces. Any low-overhead capture patterns?

maria: Bracket the hot window with NVTX ranges and capture only that. nvtxRangePushA("req-start"); ... nvtxRangePop(); keeps the trace focused. :white_check_mark:

devon: CLI pattern that works for us:
```bash
nsys profile -o nvtx_trace_new --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --sample=none --duration=60 -- python run_infer.py
```
This records full timeline but only inside NVTX markers so file size is bounded.

maria: If you still need smaller files, switch to sampling: `--sample=periodic:1000` (1ms) or `--sample=periodic:500` (0.5ms). Sampling drops per-call events but preserves kernel-level hotspots.

oscar: Practically: run short bracketed captures per build (30-90s) instead of one long one. Replay the same requests (or fixed seed) so comparison is apples-to-apples.

alex: We care about OS scheduling noise too — should I include osrt?

devon: Yes. Use `--trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt` so you can align CPU thread preemption/OSRT gaps with kernel launch deltas in the timeline.

maria: Small nit: use `--capture-range=nvtx` and be defensive about missing end-markers. Useful flags: `--capture-range=nvtx` + `--stop-on-exit` (so capture stops cleanly if process dies). Also give unique `-o` names.

eng_ci_bot: Please remember to upload raw traces to `/shared/nsys/` and run a quick `nsys stats` to get aggregate kernel times before opening UI. That helps triage on CI.

oscar: When you compare builds, either open two qdrep files side-by-side in nsys-ui or export CSVs: `nsys stats -r cuda -f csv -o buildA_kernels buildA.qdrep` and diff kernel durations/counts.

alex: Any tips for tiny, high-frequency kernels? We sometimes see many short launches that add up but sampling misses them.

maria: If tiny kernels are the suspect, you need `--sample=none` (full tracing) for short windows. Keep it bracketed to limit size. In UI, collapse by kernel name and look at total time vs call count. Also filter by `duration > 1us` etc.

devon: Another trick: instrument a high-level NVTX marker per logical request and a finer-grained NVTX around the small op you suspect. That gives you a narrow capture-within-capture to zoom in.

alex: sweet. Trying bracketed sampled runs with osrt now. Will upload traces when done and tag you.

maria: If you hit weird artifacts, paste the `nsys stats` CSV here first — quick to scan.

oscar: One last FYI: periodic:250 (0.25ms) gives great temporal resolution but blows up size. Start coarse and iterate. :mag:

alex: Thanks all — will report back.
